title: What the Bleep Do We Know
full_review:
Part documentary, part narrative, "What the Bleep Do We Know?" (Lord of the Wind Films) is an unwieldy metaphysical mishmash which wraps a loose story line about an unfulfilled wedding photographer (Marlee Matlin) around discussions of quantum physics, the intersection of science and spirituality, mind-body consciousness and the underlying nature of reality.

Directed by William Arntz, Betsy Chasse and Mark Vicente, the thought-provoking film takes a lively and novel approach to its mind-bending subject matter, incorporating slightly cheesy special effects, amusing animated segments and talking-head interviews with academics (including a woman who claims to get esoteric knowledge by channeling the spirit of a 35,000-year-old warrior) into the bare-bones story.

The movie's overriding thesis is that there is no objective "real world" out there, independent of our subjective experiences, only "waves of possibilities," the crux of its argument being that we each, in effect, create our own reality.

On a positive note, "What the Bleep" invites viewers into a deeper appreciation of the mystery and interconnectedness of the created universe.

However, the film derails into a muddled morass of pseudoscientific hokum, Gnostic mysticism and New-Age mumbo jumbo. And while the overall film remains open-minded to transcendent experiences, it is, at times, critical of traditional organized religion, pushing instead a less dogmatic brand of personal spirituality.

Because of mild sexual content and a few crude expressions, the USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-III -- adults. Not rated by the Motion Picture Association of America.
